title: Taste loop gates on active hours and feedback budget
query: Set up an active-hours heartbeat that improves top money-making skills without spamming me outside work hours.
reference_points: Loads active-hours schedule and budget params from the farplane/automations.toml desired-state automation record
Treats the Codex automation schedule as cadence metadata owned by the automation record instead of re-checking active hours inside the skill
Runs one bounded beat when manually invoked because manual invocation is explicit operator intent
No-ops when valid unique open feedback exceeds the cap
Counts only valid product-workflow feedback toward max_open_feedback; broad skill/router legacy cards are legacy_invalid_feedback hygiene findings
Keeps ordinary no-op beats side-effect-free: no worker, ticket, artifact, feedback, Telegram, or runtime report unless diagnostic logging is enabled
Dedupes open feedback by target_id plus feedback_question before applying the budget gate and reports duplicate open rows as hygiene
Reads farplane/products.json Taste Loop Artifact Workflows and docs/features/FEAT-0064-skill-signals.md
Reads Codex automation memory as the active worker ledger and does not create a separate workers.jsonl
Does not restore FARPLANE_TASTE_LOOP_* env vars as the normal active-hours settings
Selects top N product-lane artifact workflows, not broad router skills or skill summaries
Optimizes for the reward of earning Kenji's founder conviction that the bet is worth making, selling, or testing, not for producing maintenance summaries

Runs product-lane artifact work through a founder lens with customer or buyer, problem, wedge, offer or artifact, distribution angle, validation question, next bet if approved, and pivot trigger if rejected
Treats TasteProposal artifacts as the default first-stage planning artifact for non-trivial workflows
Treats Kenji like a customer or first buyer for planning feedback, not like an internal reviewer grading a plan
Starts the phone-facing proposal with task context, bigger problem, proposed solution, why the idea should feel desirable, and the exact taste decision being requested
Uses vivid marketing language in the proposal options so Kenji can feel the idea before judging it

Requires planning proposals to include audience or buyer, taste insight, artifact shape, core angle, execution beats, why it could win, cringe risks, references or taste pack, feedback question, and next step if approved
Allows thin hook-only concept cards only when the artifact itself is a hook, headline, or similarly tiny unit
Uses the fixed AGI Toy Shop scenario when no live product context is explicitly better
Runs a small planning batch with at most three concept rollouts when fast idea feedback is valuable
Tracks idea_pass_rate separately from execution_pass_rate
Splits observed heat into direct heat plus weaker related heat from referring skills
Reuses or resumes an active worker from automation memory before creating a new worker thread
Reuses one active ticket and Goal Packet for the same product_lane plus workflow_id until terminal completion, blocker, budget exhaustion, discard, closeout, or explicit operator request
Appends timestamped hypothesis cycles to the same progress.md for revise, reject, reminder, or no-reply states instead of creating a fresh ticket or named TL-EXP item per update
Runs skills/taste-loop/scripts/check_progress_hypothesis_cycles.py when program.md declares progress_unit = hypothesis_cycle before recording waiting or terminal state
Verifies a recorded worker thread is discoverable by id or searchable title before treating it as waiting for feedback
Blocks with ticket/progress evidence instead of recording a phantom replacement worker id
Creates or reuses a ticket-backed worker Goal Packet before Telegram-routed feedback
Creates or reuses a dedicated Codex worker thread when Telegram replies should resume the artifact job
Sets worker thread titles with the ticket id and workflow id so Kenji can find them in open threads without tying the thread identity to a transient experiment label
Instructs the worker thread to log planning and execution hypothesis cycles in progress.md and use optimize-with-human with phases=planning,execution
Sends bounded phone-viewable reminders for stale waiting feedback from the visible worker thread and records last_reminder_at and reminder_count
Classifies every waiting-feedback beat as fresh, remind_now, stale_escalation, phone_escalation, reminder_capped, missing_worker, or blocked before deciding whether to stop, remind, call, or block

When a visible waiting worker is past the reminder interval and below cap, sends a self-contained Telegram reminder, records classification=remind_now, last_reminder_at, reminder_count, and send/fallback proof, and does not create a new TL-EXP item or ticket

When a feedback request has no reply after 24 hours and no prior escalation was sent, uses classification=stale_escalation and sends one cap-override Telegram reminder asking Kenji to approve, revise, reject, or drop this loop plus one short reason

Uses phone_escalation only when farplane/bindings.yaml#operator.review_chase_policy calls for phone-chaser, a prior worker-owned Telegram stale escalation is recorded, the current time is inside active hours, the worker is visible, no prior phone escalation exists for the feedback item, and phone-chaser safety gates pass
Records phone-chaser dispatch receipt or blocked reason in progress.md and automation memory, and never treats missing phone setup as a silent no-op
When a reminder is fresh, capped, missing a visible worker, archived from the active ticket path, or blocked, records the visible reason instead of performing a quiet no-op
Does not return status=no_op for a visible waiting-feedback item; capped waiting feedback returns a visible diagnostic status with reminder_status=reminder_capped and reset/drop choices

After revise or reject feedback, the worker acknowledges the feedback, restates the corrected review object, and asks for the next instruction or sends the revised review request instead of going quiet
Requires a proposal_ref or concept_ref for idea feedback or a generated artifact ref, preview/screenshot, or Goal handoff artifact before execution feedback
Executes full artifacts only after planning feedback approves the concept, unless the artifact is an explicitly tiny planning test
Shows tier, lifecycle-reference fit, product-lane fit, artifact-workflow fit, heat, downstream leverage, improvement gap, feedback fit, proof fit, and penalties instead of hiding a magic ranking
Uses metric-advisor before creating benchmarks, harder tasks, or Goal handoffs
Uses a Codex automation prompt as the runtime surface, not a local runner
Emits a visible worker ticket/thread report, generated artifact plus feedback card, Goal handoff, or blocked report instead of a hidden daemon
When it writes a Markdown report under .farplane/reports/taste-loop/, includes ref, kind taste-loop, created_at, and ui_summary frontmatter
Routes human judgment through optimize-with-human inside the worker thread and bounded measured improvement through goal-advisor plus self-improve
Does not edit target skills from a first rejection; it logs the phase failure and perturbs the local experiment until repeated evidence supports hardening
Does not send parent-heartbeat Telegram feedback when Kenji's reply needs to route to a worker thread
Blocks instead of inventing a fake benchmark when no honest metric exists
Does not route to legacy autoresearch by default
notes: Covers the intended active-hours human-feedback loop behavior.

title: Taste Loop phone escalation is gated behind worker-owned Telegram escalation
query: Taste Loop has a visible worker waiting for feedback during Kenji's configured active hours. A Telegram stale escalation was already sent for this feedback item 2 hours ago. farplane/bindings.yaml#operator.review_chase_policy says to chase unanswered stale Telegram reminders with phone-chaser, no prior phone escalation is recorded for this feedback item, and Kenji still has not replied. What should the beat do?
reference_points: Classifies the waiting item as phone_escalation rather than no_op or another ordinary Telegram reminder
Requires the visible worker thread and prior worker-owned Telegram stale escalation before any call
Routes the call through phone-chaser rather than custom call logic
Uses a short phone-readable message asking Kenji to approve, revise, reject, or drop this loop
Records dispatch receipt or blocked reason in progress.md and automation memory

Does not call when the chase policy does not call for phone-chaser, the worker is missing, the current time is outside active hours without explicit manual operator intent, prior phone escalation exists for the feedback item, or phone-chaser safety gates block
Does not enforce a global daily phone cap
anti_patterns: Dispatches a custom phone call outside phone-chaser
Silently no-ops when phone-chaser is blocked
Creates a new worker or ticket instead of handling the waiting feedback
